 Marquez at match point in MotoGP as he seeks 14
 AFP, PORTIMAO, Portugal 
 Add TT as Preferred Source 
 Marc Marquez has a date with history this weekend, when he can retain his MotoGP crown at the Portuguese Grand Prix and in the process claim a record-equaling eighth world title in the premier class of motorcycling, 13 years after his first.
 Just 14 points from the final two race weekends, in Portimao and then Valencia, will be enough for Ducati’s Marquez to draw level with Giacomo Agostini, who won his 500cc championships between 1966 and 1975.
 Marquez could seal the deal as early as today if he wins the sprint race, but with a 60-point gap separating him from his closest rival and compatriot Jorge Martin, it would need a total disaster for him to not finish top of the pile come the end of next weekend in Spain.
 Ducati rider Marc Marquez arrives for a news conference ahead of the MotoGP Portugal Grand Prix at the Algarve circuit in Portimao on Thursday.
 Photo: AFP
 Marco Bezzecchi is still technically in the fight, but trailing by 74, the Italian needs maximum points from Portimao and Marquez to not score any to stay in it.
 “It’s true that we are in a very good situation, but in MotoGP everything can happen... We have many different moments over a race weekend,” Marquez said on Thursday. “I have a number in my mind which is 14, 14 points. If I achieve 14 points in the next two weekends, this weekend and Valencia, it doesn’t matter what the others do.”
 Marquez’s record in the sprint races gives him a good chance of heading into tomorrow’s Grand Prix already this year’s champion, with 10 wins and four other podiums so far.
 That is in comparison with seven wins and one other podium finish in the actual GPs, in a year in which he has not dominated quite like he did last season, when he won his first title in six years with five rounds remaining.
 Marquez became the youngest ever MotoGP champion in his debut season in 2013 and then went on to win the title in five of the next six seasons.
 He wants to make up for the time he lost to injury as he heads into his mid-30s.
 “The life of an athlete is short so you need to take the maximum,” he said. The “fastest Marc was 2013, [20]14, even [20]19. The best Marc is now, 100 percent. I would have liked to have the mentality I have now at 20 years old.”
